title: Direct Identification through PII Collection
description: Registration collects personally identifiable information (name, email, government ID) that directly identifies the parent user, creating inherent identifiability risk.

title: Unauthorized Disclosure of Sensitive Government ID
description: Government ID is highly sensitive personal data that, if disclosed to unauthorized parties, could lead to identity theft, fraud, or other privacy violations.

title: Excessive Data Collection for Authentication
description: Collecting government ID and six-digit code may exceed data minimization principles for authentication purposes, potentially collecting more data than necessary.

title: Linkability of Registration Data to External Sources
description: Email and government ID could be linked to other databases or services, potentially enabling correlation of the parent user's activities across different systems.

title: Unauthorized access to parent account data
description: MongoDB users collection storing parent account information may be accessible to unauthorized parties through database vulnerabilities, misconfiguration, or insufficient access controls.

title: Identification of users from parent account data
description: Parent account information stored in the authentication service could be used to identify specific individuals, potentially revealing personal relationships or family structures.

title: Tampering with authentication data
description: Parent account information in the authentication service could be altered by malicious actors, potentially affecting authentication integrity and user access.

title: Impersonation using parent account credentials
description: Parent account authentication credentials could be stolen or compromised, allowing unauthorized individuals to impersonate legitimate users.

title: User Identifiability via JWT Token
description: The JWT token sent to the parent user contains user identity information that could be used to identify the individual, especially if the token is intercepted or leaked.
assumptions: JWT contains PII or unique identifiers

title: User Data Disclosure During Transmission
description: User data transmitted alongside the JWT could be disclosed to unauthorized parties if the communication channel is not properly secured (e.g., no TLS encryption).
assumptions: Transmission may not be encrypted

title: JWT Token Theft and Usurpation
description: If the JWT token is stolen or intercepted, an attacker could potentially usurp the user's identity and access protected resources on behalf of the parent user.
assumptions: JWT is not short-lived or properly validated

title: Excessive User Data in JWT
description: The JWT may contain more user data than necessary for the parent user to perform their function, violating data minimization principles.
assumptions: JWT includes unnecessary claims

title: Linkability of User Data Across Systems
description: The parent user (EE1) may be able to link the received user data with other data sources, creating a comprehensive profile of the individual.
assumptions: Parent user has access to other data sources

title: Linkability of Child Login to Parent Identity
description: Child's login activity using parent credentials can be linked to the parent's identity through the parent email, creating a connection between child and parent data across systems.
assumptions: Parent email is stored and accessible in the system

title: Identification of Parent-Child Relationship
description: The use of parent email and password for child authentication reveals the parent-child relationship, potentially identifying both individuals.
assumptions: Parent email is unique and identifiable

title: Disclosure of Parent Credentials in Transit
description: Parent email and password transmitted during child login could be intercepted by attackers, leading to credential compromise.
assumptions: Transmission may not be fully encrypted or could be vulnerable to interception

title: Excessive Data Collection for Child Authentication
description: Collecting parent email and password for child login may exceed data minimization principles, as child-specific credentials could be used instead.
assumptions: Child-specific authentication is technically feasible

title: Usurpation of Child Identity via Parent Credentials
description: If parent credentials are compromised, unauthorized parties could impersonate the child or parent, leading to identity usurpation.
assumptions: Parent credentials could be stolen or shared

title: Non-compliance with Child Privacy Regulations
description: Using parent credentials for child authentication may violate child privacy regulations (e.g., COPPA) that require age-appropriate consent and data handling.
assumptions: Applicable child privacy laws require direct child consent
uncertainty_note: Regulatory requirements may vary by jurisdiction

title: Direct identification of child user through JWT and profile data
description: The JWT token and child profile data transmitted from the Authentication Service contains personally identifiable information that can directly identify the child user.

title: Unauthorized disclosure of JWT tokens during transmission
description: JWT tokens transmitted from the Authentication Service to the Child User could be intercepted by unauthorized parties, potentially leading to unauthorized access to the child's account.

title: Identity usurpation through stolen JWT tokens
description: If JWT tokens are intercepted or stolen, unauthorized parties could impersonate the child user to access protected resources.

title: Excessive data collection in child profiles
description: The child profile data transmitted may contain more personal information than necessary for the authentication service's purpose, violating data minimization principles.

title: Direct Identification of Child
description: The child's government ID, name, and DOB are direct identifiers that can be used to uniquely identify the child in the system.

title: Linkability of Child Data
description: The child's profile data could be linked with other data sources (e.g., school records, medical records) to create a comprehensive profile of the child.

title: Unauthorized Disclosure of Sensitive Data
description: The child's sensitive information (government ID, DOB, gender) could be disclosed to unauthorized parties during processing or storage.

title: Data Integrity Compromise
description: The child profile data could be tampered with, modified, or corrupted during processing by unauthorized actors.

title: Parent Identity Usurpation
description: An attacker could impersonate the parent user to create or modify child profiles, potentially enrolling a child without consent.

title: Regulatory Non-Compliance
description: The data processing may not comply with child data protection regulations (e.g., COPPA, GDPR-K) regarding consent, data minimization, and parental rights.

title: Unauthorized disclosure of child profile data
description: Child profile data stored in MongoDB could be accessed or disclosed to unauthorized parties through inadequate access controls, data breaches, or improper data sharing mechanisms.

title: Unauthorized modification of child profile data
description: Child profile data could be tampered with by unauthorized actors, leading to incorrect or malicious alterations of sensitive child information.

title: Identification of children from stored profiles
description: Stored child profile data could be used to identify individual children, potentially exposing them to privacy risks and enabling tracking across systems.

title: Unauthorized impersonation during profile updates
description: Unauthorized actors could impersonate children or parents to make changes to child profiles, potentially leading to fraudulent or harmful modifications.

title: Regulatory non-compliance for child data
description: The child profile management process may fail to comply with child-specific data protection regulations such as COPPA, GDPR-K, or other applicable laws regarding consent, data minimization, and parental rights.

title: Linkability of Video Search and Interaction History
description: Child User's video search queries, likes, and comments can be linked across sessions and contexts, potentially revealing patterns of interest and behavior that could be used to build a profile of the user.
assumptions: User activities are logged and stored in a persistent manner

title: Identification Through Behavioral Patterns
description: Video search patterns, comment content, and like behavior could be used to identify the Child User, especially if combined with other data sources or if the user is unique in their viewing preferences.
assumptions: User behavior is distinctive enough to enable identification

title: Disclosure of Video Content and User Interactions
description: Video content accessed through the search and request functionality, along with user comments and likes, could be disclosed to unauthorized parties through data breaches, improper access controls, or sharing mechanisms.
assumptions: Video content and interaction data are stored and potentially accessible to unauthorized actors

title: Excessive Collection of User Interaction Data
description: The Video Management Service may collect excessive data including detailed search history, comment content, and like patterns that exceeds what is necessary for the core functionality of video search, request, like, and comment features.
assumptions: Data collection practices are not minimized to what is strictly necessary

title: Usurpation Through Account Compromise
description: If the Child User's account is compromised, an attacker could impersonate the user to post comments, like videos, or search for content on their behalf, leading to unauthorized actions and potential reputation damage.
assumptions: User authentication mechanisms may be vulnerable to compromise

title: Non-Compliance with Privacy Regulations
description: The Video Management Service may fail to comply with privacy regulations (e.g., GDPR, COPPA) regarding collection, storage, and processing of video search and interaction data from the Child User, especially concerning age-appropriate data handling.
assumptions: Regulatory requirements may not be fully implemented or enforced

title: Video metadata linked to individuals
description: Video metadata (timestamps, locations, user IDs) could be linked to specific individuals, enabling tracking of their activities across time and space.
assumptions: Metadata contains or can be correlated with personally identifiable information

title: Video content reveals identity
description: Video files may contain visual or audio content that directly identifies individuals (faces, voices, biometric data), potentially exposing private information.
assumptions: Videos contain identifiable content of individuals

title: Unauthorized access to video files
description: MongoDB collection may be accessible by unauthorized parties, leading to exposure of video content and metadata to individuals without proper authorization.
assumptions: Inadequate access controls on MongoDB or network vulnerabilities

title: Excessive video data collection
description: System may collect video files and metadata beyond what is necessary for the stated purpose, violating data minimization principles.
assumptions: Video storage requirements exceed functional needs

title: Unauthorized video upload or access
description: Without proper authentication, unauthorized users could upload videos or access existing videos, leading to privacy violations and potential misuse.
assumptions: Authentication mechanisms are weak or bypassed

title: Child Identifiability from Search/Watch History
description: Search and watch history stored in child profiles could be used to identify the child's identity, interests, and behavioral patterns, potentially revealing sensitive personal information about the child.
assumptions: The data is stored in a manner that allows correlation with other identifying information
uncertainty_note: Using I.1.1 as a general identifiability node; specific LINDDUN Pro tree structure may vary

title: Unauthorized Disclosure of Child Profile Data
description: Child search and watch history could be disclosed to unauthorized parties including other users, third-party services, or even unauthorized family members without proper consent mechanisms.
assumptions: Access controls are not properly implemented or are bypassed
uncertainty_note: D.1.1 is a general disclosure node; specific context may require different sub-node

title: Linkability of Child Data Across Systems
description: Child search and watch history could be linked with other data sources (e.g., parental accounts, device identifiers, location data) to create comprehensive profiles of the child's activities and preferences.
assumptions: Data exists in multiple systems that can be correlated
uncertainty_note: L.1.1 is a general linkability node; specific threat-tree may have more granular options

title: Data Integrity Compromise of Child History
description: The MongoDB childprofiles collection storing search and watch history could be tampered with, altered, or deleted by unauthorized actors, leading to inaccurate records of child's activities.
assumptions: The data store lacks proper integrity controls and audit mechanisms
uncertainty_note: Dd.1.1 is a general data integrity node; specific LINDDUN Pro structure may vary

title: Regulatory Non-Compliance for Children's Data
description: Storing child search and watch history may violate GDPR, COPPA, or other child privacy regulations regarding data minimization, parental consent, and data retention requirements.
assumptions: Data collection and storage practices do not meet applicable legal requirements
uncertainty_note: Nc.1.1 is a general non-compliance node; specific regulatory context may require different classification

title: Video Content Identifies User
description: Video data inherently contains identifiable information about the user, including facial features, voice, and personal context, making the user directly identifiable from the uploaded content.

title: Unauthorized Video Disclosure
description: Video data may be disclosed to unauthorized parties during storage, processing, or transmission within the Video Management Service, potentially exposing sensitive personal information.

title: Video Data Tampering
description: Video data could be altered or tampered with during the upload or approval/rejection process, compromising data integrity and potentially creating false evidence.

title: Cross-Context Linkability
description: Video data could be linked to the user across different systems or time periods, enabling profiling and tracking of user behavior beyond the immediate context.

title: Approval Process Usability Issues
description: The approval/rejection workflow may be difficult to use or understand, potentially leading to privacy-related errors or user frustration that could result in unintended data exposure.

title: Child Identifiable from Video Stream
description: The video stream contains visual content that can identify the child user, potentially exposing their identity to unauthorized observers.

title: Video Stream Disclosure to Unauthorized Parties
description: The video stream could be intercepted, recorded, or accessed by unauthorized third parties during transmission or storage.

title: Video Stream Linkable to Child Identity
description: The video content can be linked to the child's identity through metadata, timestamps, or contextual information, enabling profiling.

title: Regulatory Non-Compliance with Children's Privacy Laws
description: Streaming video to a child may violate regulations such as COPPA or GDPR-K regarding children's data protection and consent requirements.

title: Child Identifiability from Profile Data
description: Child profiles in MongoDB collection contain personally identifiable information that could directly or indirectly identify children, violating privacy expectations for minors.

title: Unauthorized Disclosure of Child Browsing Data
description: Child browsing data could be accessed by unauthorized parties through inadequate access controls, leading to privacy violations and potential exploitation.

title: Regulatory Non-Compliance for Child Data
description: Child data processing may violate COPPA, GDPR-K, or other child privacy regulations due to insufficient consent mechanisms and data protection measures.

title: Linkability of Child Data Across Systems
description: AI Recommendation Engine could link child browsing data with other datasets, creating comprehensive profiles that increase identifiability risks.

title: Unauthorized Use of Child Data for AI Training
description: Child browsing data could be used to train AI models without proper parental consent, violating child privacy rights and regulatory requirements.

title: AI-Generated Misleading Recommendations
description: AI Recommendation Engine could generate manipulative or age-inappropriate content recommendations based on child browsing patterns, deceiving children about content suitability.

title: Linkability of browsing data to individual users
description: Browsing data sent to third-party advertisers may be linked to specific individuals, enabling tracking across sessions and devices.
assumptions: Advertisers have access to additional identifiers that can correlate browsing data with user identities.

title: Identifiability of users from browsing patterns
description: Browsing data can be used to infer or directly identify individual users, revealing personal interests, habits, and potentially sensitive information.
assumptions: Advertisers can analyze browsing patterns to build user profiles that identify individuals.

title: Over-disclosure of browsing data to advertisers
description: More browsing data may be shared with advertisers than necessary for the intended purpose, exposing users to unnecessary privacy risks.
assumptions: Data minimization principles are not followed; excessive data is transmitted.

title: Deception about data usage and purposes
description: Users may not be fully informed about how their browsing data will be used by third-party advertisers, leading to consent without understanding.
assumptions: Privacy policies are vague or users do not read them; data usage extends beyond stated purposes.

title: Non-compliance with privacy regulations
description: Sharing browsing data with third-party advertisers may violate GDPR, CCPA, or other privacy regulations if proper consent and data protection measures are not in place.
assumptions: Regulatory requirements for third-party data sharing are not met; consent mechanisms are inadequate.

title: Direct Identification of Data Subjects
description: Government ID images contain personally identifiable information that directly identifies individuals, making them highly sensitive to identification attacks.

title: Linkability of ID Images to Other Data Sources
description: Stored government ID images can be linked to other datasets (e.g., transaction records, biometric data) creating comprehensive profiles of individuals.

title: Unauthorized Disclosure of ID Images
description: File system storing government ID images may be accessed by unauthorized parties through inadequate access controls or security vulnerabilities.

title: Data Manipulation of Stored ID Images
description: ID images in the file system could be altered, tampered with, or replaced by malicious actors, compromising data integrity.

title: Identity Usurpation via Stolen ID Images
description: If ID images are compromised, attackers could use them to impersonate individuals and gain unauthorized access to systems or services.

title: Non-Compliance with Privacy Regulations
description: Storing government ID images may violate GDPR, CCPA, or other privacy regulations if proper consent, retention policies, and security measures are not implemented.

title: JWT Token Disclosure via XSS
description: JWT tokens stored in localStorage are accessible to any JavaScript running on the page, making them vulnerable to Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) attacks. An attacker with XSS access can read and exfiltrate the JWT token.
assumptions: Vulnerable to XSS due to localStorage accessibility

title: Session Hijacking via Stolen JWT
description: If a JWT token is stolen from localStorage (e.g., via XSS, network sniffing, or malicious browser extension), an attacker can use it to impersonate the authenticated user and gain unauthorized access to protected resources.
assumptions: JWT contains valid authentication claims and is not short-lived

title: User Identifiability from JWT Claims
description: JWT tokens often contain user identifiers (sub, email, user_id) in their claims. If exposed, these can be used to identify and profile the user across systems.
assumptions: JWT contains identifiable user information in claims

title: JWT Token Tampering
description: Since localStorage is mutable via JavaScript, an attacker with access can modify the JWT token contents, potentially altering user roles, permissions, or other claims to escalate privileges.
assumptions: JWT is not cryptographically signed or is using weak signature

title: Linkability of Authentication Events
description: The authentication service can link multiple authentication events to the same user session via the JWT, potentially creating a detailed profile of user behavior across different services.
assumptions: Authentication service maintains session logs

title: Child Identifiability from History Data
description: Child history data retrieved for parent review contains personally identifiable information that could identify the child, including names, dates of events, and potentially sensitive health or behavioral information.

title: Unauthorized Access to Child History
description: Child history data may be accessed by unauthorized parties if the parent user authentication is compromised or if data is transmitted without proper encryption.

title: Parent User Impersonation
description: An unauthorized individual could impersonate the parent user to access child history data, potentially through weak authentication mechanisms or credential theft.

title: Excessive Data Collection in Child History
description: Child history may contain more data than necessary for parent review purposes, including sensitive information that exceeds what is needed for legitimate parental oversight.

title: Linkability of Child History to Other Records
description: Child history data could be linked with other data sources about the child or family, creating a comprehensive profile that increases privacy risks.
